reason: Gate A improvement: a PR must declare ALL its completed work records (windows + stories), not exactly one — strengthens traceability and makes review-driven multi-window PRs first-class

quality.summary: Reviewed the Gate A contract change (lite window Q-0043-cbbc). check_pr_ticket.py's resolution is rewritten from 'exactly one resolved' to set logic: completed = done-flipped stories (with added history) + added window done-records; the gate passes iff completed is non-empty AND every completed record's key is declared (Ticket: line or feat/<key>- branch). Clean and direct: single-record PRs behave identically (verified by the unchanged passing tests), the new failure is a completed-but-undeclared record, and extra non-resolving declarations are ignored. Messages name the undeclared records. Tests updated coherently: the former two-resolved-fails test now asserts two-declared passes, plus a new test pinning one-of-two-declared fails. Decision 0033 documents the contract. No over-engineering.

performance.summary: Set operations over the small completed/candidates sets in a CI-only script that already walks the diff. No runtime hot path, no added I/O, no measurable cost.

security.summary: This is an integrity-gate STRENGTHENING: it closes a traceability loophole where a PR completing multiple work records could pass while declaring only one, leaving the rest undeclared. The new contract fails any completed-but-undeclared record, so every merged change stays accounted for. No new trust boundary, input surface, or data flow; the gate remains a read-only check over the diff. Consistent with 0009 (the harness evolves its own gate via a decision; clients get it frozen on vendoring).
